【P8｜Dr. Lanyon】
别称：HASTIE LANYON、Lanyon
当前一句话身份：Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
档案（最新）：occupation：doctor and colleague of Jekyll；appearance：pale, balder, older, visibly decaying；personality：Cautious, suspicious of Jekyll's sanity；situation：life shaken, sleepless, believes he must die；alive：dead；residence：Cavendish Square
关系：Mr. Utterson（friend and recipient）、Dr. Jekyll（受托取药之人）、the carpenter（craftsman）、the locksmith（craftsman）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Utterson goes to Cavendish Square to consult his friend Dr. Lanyon.
- Utterson asks whether he and Lanyon are Jekyll's two oldest friends.
- Lanyon says Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago.
- Utterson asks Lanyon about Hyde, and Lanyon has never heard of him.
- Jekyll calls Lanyon a hide-bound pedant and says he was disappointed in him.
- Utterson dines with Jekyll and Lanyon as inseparable friends.
- Utterson visits Lanyon and is shocked by his decayed appearance.
- Lanyon declares himself a doomed man who will never recover.
- Lanyon refuses to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him.
- Lanyon takes to his bed and dies within a fortnight.
- After the funeral Utterson opens Lanyon's sealed envelope.
- Lanyon receives a registered letter from Henry Jekyll on the ninth of January.
- Jekyll begs Lanyon to help him, saying his life and reason are at stake.
- Jekyll instructs Lanyon to force open his cabinet and take the fourth drawer.
- Jekyll asks Lanyon to receive a midnight messenger and hand over the drawer.
- Lanyon suspects Jekyll is insane but feels bound to obey the appeal.
- Lanyon drives to Jekyll's house, where the butler awaits him.
- The carpenter and locksmith work two hours to open Jekyll's cabinet door.
- Lanyon takes the drawer, has it packed in straw and a sheet, and returns home.
- Lanyon examines the drawer's powders, phial, and book of dated experiments.
- Lanyon dismisses his servants and loads an old revolver for self-defence.
- At midnight a small man knocks gently and crouches against the portico pillars.
- Lanyon asks if the visitor comes from Dr. Jekyll, and the man gestures yes.
- Lanyon sees the visitor clearly for the first time and is struck by his appearance.
- Hyde enters Lanyon's house and urgently asks if he has it
- Lanyon rebukes Hyde for forgetting they are unacquainted
- Lanyon points Hyde to the drawer holding the package
- Hyde uncovers the contents and sobs with immense relief
- Hyde mixes the red tincture and powder into a changing compound
- Hyde offers Lanyon knowledge and power or to leave unwiser
- Lanyon agrees to see the end of the inexplicable service
- Hyde drinks the glass at one gulp and cries out
- Hyde transforms and Henry Jekyll stands before Lanyon
- Jekyll confesses his moral turpitude to Lanyon with tears
- Lanyon learns the visitor was Hyde, murderer of Carew

【P7｜Dr. Jekyll】
别称：Dr. Henry Jekyll、Dr. J.、Edward Hyde、H.J.、HENRY JEKYLL、Harry
当前一句话身份：Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
档案（最新）：appearance：never photographed; described differently by observers；personality：known for charities and religion；situation：hunted across the land as Carew's murderer；identity：Lanyon's colleague and doctor；residence：house with laboratory and cabinet；age：fifty；alive：dead
关系：Mr. Utterson（lawyer who knew him）、Dr. Lanyon（受托医生）、Poole（servant）、the old woman（landlady）、Sir Danvers Carew（the one harmed）、Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard（accuser）
至今经历（按时间）：
- The maid sees Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane.
- Utterson recognizes the stick as one he gave Henry Jekyll.
- The inspector finds several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank.
- The inspector plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.
- Mr. Hyde had few familiars and was hard to trace.
- Hyde's family could not be traced anywhere.
- Hyde had never been photographed.
- Observers agreed only on a sense of unexpressed deformity in Hyde.
- Utterson is admitted by Poole and received into Jekyll's cabinet.
- Jekyll swears he will never set eyes on Hyde again.
- Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde to judge.
- Jekyll says he burned the envelope and it bore no postmark.
- Jekyll admits Hyde dictated the terms of his will.
- Hyde vanishes after Sir Danvers's murder; rewards are offered.
- Jekyll emerges from seclusion and resumes his old friendships.
- Utterson dines with Jekyll and Lanyon as inseparable friends.
- Jekyll shuts his door against Utterson, Poole reporting he is confined.
- Utterson writes to Jekyll, who replies of an incurable quarrel.
- Jekyll vows extreme seclusion and speaks of an unnameable punishment.
- The enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance.
- Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.
- Utterson sees Dr. Jekyll sitting sadly at the middle window.
- Jekyll replies he is very low and says it will not last long.
- Utterson introduces his cousin Mr. Enfield to Dr. Jekyll and invites Jekyll out.
- Jekyll declines the walk, saying it is quite impossible and he dare not.
- Jekyll's smile turns to abject terror and the window is thrust down.
- Lanyon receives a registered letter from Henry Jekyll on the ninth of January.
- Jekyll begs Lanyon to help him, saying his life and reason are at stake.
- Jekyll orders Poole to wait with a locksmith for Lanyon's arrival.
- Jekyll instructs Lanyon to force open his cabinet and take the fourth drawer.
- Jekyll asks Lanyon to receive a midnight messenger and hand over the drawer.
- Jekyll warns that if the night passes without event, Lanyon has seen the last of him.
- Lanyon suspects Jekyll is insane but feels bound to obey the appeal.
- Hyde enters Lanyon's house and urgently asks if he has it
- Lanyon rebukes Hyde for forgetting they are unacquainted
- Hyde says he comes at the instance of Dr. Henry Jekyll
- Lanyon points Hyde to the drawer holding the package
- Hyde uncovers the contents and sobs with immense relief
- Hyde mixes the red tincture and powder into a changing compound
- Hyde offers Lanyon knowledge and power or to leave unwiser
- Lanyon agrees to see the end of the inexplicable service
- Hyde drinks the glass at one gulp and cries out
- Hyde transforms and Henry Jekyll stands before Lanyon
- Jekyll confesses his moral turpitude to Lanyon with tears
- Lanyon learns the visitor was Hyde, murderer of Carew

【P22｜the small man】
别称：a small man
当前一句话身份：Small man who comes at midnight in Jekyll's name
档案（最新）：appearance：Small, with shocking facial expression；situation：Comes secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name
关系：无
至今经历（按时间）：
- At midnight a small man knocks gently and crouches against the portico pillars.
- Lanyon asks if the visitor comes from Dr. Jekyll, and the man gestures yes.
- The visitor glances back at a policeman and hurries inside.
- Lanyon sees the visitor clearly for the first time and is struck by his appearance.

【P10｜Poole】
别称：无
当前一句话身份：Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
档案（最新）：occupation：Jekyll's butler；situation：afraid for about a week, cannot bear it；appearance：white face, harsh broken voice
关系：Dr. Jekyll（obeyed superior）、the housemaid（subordinate）、the cook（subordinate）、the knife-boy（subordinate）、the voice（master）、Mr. Utterson（lawyer directing the search）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Poole tells Utterson that Dr. Jekyll has gone out.
- Poole confirms Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door.
- Poole says all servants have orders to obey Hyde.
- Poole says Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory.
- Utterson is admitted by Poole and received into Jekyll's cabinet.
- Poole tells Utterson no letter came except by post.
- Jekyll shuts his door against Utterson, Poole reporting he is confined.
- Utterson prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.
- Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.
- Poole comes to Utterson's house at night and says something is wrong.
- Poole says the doctor has shut himself in the cabinet and he is afraid.
- Poole says he thinks there has been foul play.
- Utterson rises, takes hat and greatcoat, and follows Poole.
- They enter the hall where all the servants are huddled in fear.
- Poole leads Utterson to the laboratory and tells him to listen quietly.
- Poole knocks and calls that Utterson asks to see him.
- Poole asks whether that was his master's voice; Utterson says it seems much changed.
- Poole declares his master was made away with eight days ago.
- Utterson calls the tale wild and argues a murderer would not stay.
- Poole tells of a week of notes demanding a pure drug from chemists.
- Poole hands Utterson a crumpled note from Dr. Jekyll to Messrs. Maw.
- Utterson notes the handwriting is the doctor's; Poole says he has seen him.
- Poole tells Utterson he saw a masked figure in the cabinet.
- Poole insists the masked thing was not Jekyll but a dwarf.
- Poole and Utterson agree to break in together.
- Utterson warns Poole they are placing themselves in peril.
- Poole says the masked figure was Mr. Hyde.
- Poole and Utterson wait in the theatre and hear pacing footsteps.
- Poole says the walker weeps like a woman or lost soul.
- Poole strikes the door five times with the axe until it bursts.
- They peer in and find the contorted body of Edward Hyde.
- Utterson and Poole search the theatre, cabinet, closets and cellar for Jekyll.
- They find the by-street door locked with a rusty broken key lying nearby.
- They find a pious book annotated by Jekyll with startling blasphemies.
- Utterson reads Jekyll's dated note and concludes Jekyll was alive that day and may have fled.
- Poole hands Utterson a sealed packet, the third enclosure.
- Utterson decides to go home, read the documents, and return before midnight to send for the police.
- Jekyll orders Poole to wait with a locksmith for Lanyon's arrival.
- Lanyon drives to Jekyll's house, where the butler awaits him.

[note_g1]
Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor.。Hastie Lanyon is a doctor and colleague of Henry Jekyll, and an old friend of Mr. Utterson. He is cautious and suspicious of Jekyll's sanity. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind, and later refused to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him. After dining with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, he was shocked by his own decayed appearance and declared himself a doomed man who would never recover. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened his sealed envelope.

[note_g2]
Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir.。Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, colleague of Dr. Lanyon, and lawyer Utterson's acquaintance, known for charities and religion. He is hunted across the land as Carew's murderer. He swore never to set eyes on Hyde again, admitted Hyde dictated his will, and after Hyde vanished resumed his old friendships. He then shut his door against Utterson, vowed extreme seclusion, and spoke of an unnameable punishment. On the ninth of January he begged Lanyon to force open his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and receive a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeyed, and Jekyll confessed his moral turpitude with tears.

[note_g3]
Small man who comes at midnight in Jekyll's name.。The small man is a secret midnight visitor who comes in Dr. Jekyll's name to Dr. Lanyon's house. He is small, with a shocking facial expression. At midnight he knocked gently and crouched against the portico pillars; when Lanyon asked if he came from Dr. Jekyll, he gestured yes. He glanced back at a policeman and hurried inside. Lanyon then saw him clearly for the first time and was struck by his appearance. He is currently at Lanyon's house, having come secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name.

[note_g4]
